specification.objective: Prepare the Magi 1.8.1 patch-version metadata and release notes for the reviewed profile-local Agent/Dashboard IPC bridge and accumulated unreleased Desktop redesign, without changing runtime behavior.

requirements.statement: All authoritative plugin, npm test-package, README, and current compatibility-document version fields consistently report 1.8.1.
The 1.8.1 changelog section dated 2026-10-26 includes the accumulated Desktop redesign and the profile-local AI IPC bridge; prior 1.8.0 and older release notes remain intact.
Version metadata changes do not modify runtime behavior; the existing CI suite remains green and its release metadata test verifies the version sources and changelog.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Manifest, package.json, package-lock root entries, README and both current compatibility-document titles all agree on 1.8.1.
The dated 1.8.1 changelog preserves the Unreleased Desktop redesign and documents the IPC bridge while retaining historical sections.
The full repository CI suite passes against the version-bumped tree with no runtime code changes.

invariants.statement: No runtime/plugin logic, dependencies, Hermes configuration, credentials, or memory data are changed.
No release tag or GitHub release is created; only source metadata and notes are prepared.

forbidden_states.statement: Version sources disagree or historical changelog sections are lost.
The metadata update changes runtime behavior, dependencies, Hermes configuration, or creates a release tag.

inputs.statement: User requests a version bump, commit, and push after independent review approval of the IPC implementation.
The latest published source tag is v1.8.0; four source commits and an Unreleased Desktop redesign currently follow it.
The IPC bridge implementation was independently reviewed and validated before this metadata-only change.

outputs.statement: Consistent Magi 1.8.1 source version metadata and dated release notes, validated without changing runtime behavior.

failure_semantics.statement: If version consistency or full CI validation fails, do not commit or publish the metadata change.
